stem: What is the recommended technique for removing a non-battery foreign body from a child’s nose with a curette?

options.text: Push the object medially then rotate it out
Insert the curette above the object, pull down, then pull forward
Use a twisting motion to screw the curette into the object
Apply suction directly to the front of the object
Grasp the object with forceps and pull straight out

explanation: Insert the curette above the object, pull down, then pull forward is the correct technique for hooking a nasal foreign body and removing it safely.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because pushing the object can drive it deeper into the nasal cavity and increase the risk of trauma or aspiration.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because placing the curette above the object and then drawing it down and forward hooks the foreign body and brings it out of the nostril.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a twisting motion is more likely to dislodge the object unpredictably or injure the nasal mucosa.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because suction is not the recommended curette technique for this manoeuvre and may not effectively engage the object.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because forceps are not the described tool for this mechanical curette technique and straight traction may push the object posteriorly.

source.hint: The technique involves moving the instrument behind the object to create leverage.
